correctness.rationale: For each dual edge pair a,b in (0,1], the original circular and replacement elliptic height graphs have descending slopes m_R=x/sqrt(1-b²/4-x²), m_E=c*x/sqrt(c²-x²). Squaring gives m_R>m_E exactly for 0<x<a/2. Integration of sqrt(1+m²) gives E_A<C_A; symmetry gives E_B<C_B. The exact midpoint height difference a²b²/[16(1+r_A)(r_A+h)(1+h)] and the strict 1-Lipschitz graph-length inequality imply 0<C_A-E_A<b/8<E_B, and symmetrically C_B-E_B<E_A. Thus max(C_A,C_B)<E_A+E_B<C_A+C_B. Original source Sections 3–6 establish disjoint surgery regions, selected-arc support centers and smoothness off the chosen arcs, so the singular H¹ measure is the sum of selected arc lengths up to finitely many points. All-elliptic is the unique max; minimum selects a shorter original circular arc in every pair (equal-length ties permitted). Differentiation in b² under a uniformly positive denominator proves the coefficient kappa(a); independent quadrature compared six nondegenerate pairs, the midpoint identity, and kappa(a) at a=.1,.4,1 against its positive integral.

value.rationale: H¹-measure of the nonsmooth boundary is an intrinsic geometric regularity measure for constant-width solids. The theorem optimizes this invariant across the natural 3^m mixed-surgery family for every fixed standard Reuleaux polyhedron, identifying a structural tradeoff between symmetric elliptic replacement and minimal singular length. The positive quadratic coefficient gives the natural asymptotic for a degenerate dual chord, beyond merely verifying a numerical ellipse perimeter.
residual_risks: No statement about globally minimal-volume bodies, surface area or general constant-width solids.

limitations: Fixed input standard Reuleaux polyhedron; legal independent mixed surgeries only.
Degenerate short-edge asymptotic is a local configuration law.
